what: rules the child-facing gate can emit that fire ZERO times across the whole corpus, each with the reason the silence is correct. A rule at zero is either enforcing nothing or looking at nothing, and the output cannot tell you which.
rule: R1007 — a gate reports on every run including zero; a run producing no line is itself the reportable event

silent.notation: no MATHS item exists — no code path creates a MATHS questionType (R61). The rule is ENFORCING: its canary (a bare "5.00 pounds" and "4C") fires every run, so the zero is a fact about the corpus and not about the rule.
silent.us-spelling: the corpus is authored in British English and carries no US spelling. ENFORCING: its canary ("the color of the harbor") fires every run.

andHOWTHESEDIFFERFROMANINERTRULE: each has a CANARY that fires. A rule at zero whose canary does not fire is refused outright and no declaration excuses it — that is the state the subject-matter screen was in for three turns while nothing was printed.
